items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: we got a hell of a fine banjo player down there, Howdy Quicksell

ctx.x: We had a more, aloofal style, and you couldn't make the one, ours go over into their type of thing, which had been very, very successful. So they come up, they're thinking the tunes can do it. They tried, but they didn't come up with anything. The first tune we got that was like anything like what we could do was "Sunday" and then they brought us a trio. They also picked out our singers, so we had Bix Murray, Frank Bessinger, guys like that although good in their own, they were successful, weren't good with us.…

Now that's more improvising than you can get, but it's a different kind of improvising. Eddie King could probably go along with. It didn't hurt anything. So here we got Eddie right in front of the mike playing his guitar and we got a hell of a fine banjo player down there, Howdy Quicksell and

you don't even hear him. You know, they just ran roughshod over some of the things that we had that we could do. Later on we did 'My Pretty Girl' and it was liked by the musicians, which, I guess, that's what we were trying to satisfy and we were trying to make something that would impress the musicians.
